sections.text: If he worships one form alone with real faith, then shall his desires be fulfilled through that only; for thus have I ordained.
The fruit that comes to men of limited insight is, after all, finite. They who worship the Lower Powers attain them; but those who worship Me come unto Me alone.
The ignorant think of Me, who am the Unmanifested Spirit, as if I were really in human form. They do not understand that My Superior Nature is changeless and most excellent.

We have been discussing Chapter 7, the Yoga of Knowledge and Wisdom. We have seen that Bhagavan said, consciously or unconsciously, we are all seeking the Lord. We are all seeking who we are, where we came from.
Some of us seek unconsciously and some consciously. Those who seek unconsciously obviously do not know where the answer is. Those who seek consciously are worshipping the Lord, the source of their being.
We have seen that seekers can be classified into four types. Of these four, the Gnani is so firm in his conviction that his self is something other than the limited self. We need to find out what that is.
But the journey from ignorance about the self to knowing the self takes its own effort. Bahunam janmanam ante jnanavaan mam prapadyate. After many years of sincere seeking, the Gnani who is sincerely seeking his own self finds the truth.
He comes to the conclusion: Vasudevah sarvam iti -- there is nothing other than the supreme reality. There is no separate world and there is no separate I. All that exists is Vasudeva. Anything that I see, touch, feel, or perceive is nothing but that one supreme reality alone.
But Bhagavan said, why dont we all realize this? Kamaih taih taih hrita jnanah -- because of this desire and that desire, the knowledge which is inherently ours is taken away from us. And therefore we seek the fulfiller of that desire. Who do I go and meet at a party? The one I think is going to be the most beneficial to me.
Networking parties, Im talking about. Somebody may come very lovingly and say, Rajan! I say, No, no, not right now. I need to go and talk to that guy, because thats where I think my benefit lies. Even at a social party, we go say hello first to whoever we think is most important.
With this desire and that desire, our sense of who we are is looted away. And then we seek the fulfiller of that desire. Thats the Devata -- the one we consider the fulfiller.
The object of our desire becomes the Devata we worship. And Bhagavan says, whatever your desire and whoever your Devata, it eventually comes from me alone. Whatever you have faith in -- that entity, that source will fulfill your desire. I make your faith even firmer. Where does the faith come from? Faith comes from my own attachment and understanding.
My own consciousness, my own thinking, is only possible because the Supreme functions through me as consciousness. The same consciousness which allows me to think makes me think over and over in the same line of thinking. It makes my faith firmer and firmer the more I think in that line. Only science can give me the answer. The more I indulge in that thought, the firmer my faith becomes. All these sadhus and monks are nonsense. s how he started -- These guys are just bluffing their way. So the more we think in the same line, the firmer our faith becomes through our own consciousness.
Bhagawan says, I make their faith firm. And then, the more they worship that Devata, the more they fulfill that desire sincerely. Whenever I apply myself in whatever field, the success comes from that field. Bhagavan said, wherever you apply yourself with faith, your desires will be fulfilled.
However, he said, all that comes from me alone. Sa taya shraddhaya yuktah tasya aradhanam ihate labhate cha tatah kaman maya eva vihitan hi tan. No matter where you think this profit came from, where you think this success came from, no matter who you think helped you -- Bhagavan said, that was your faith making you think it came from that source.
However, because I am the all-pervading Lord, everything coming to you from these different Devatas is coming from me alone. I am the only source. Those in business, you have several accounts and LLCs.
You transfer money from here and there. Eventually, whose money is it? Yours. Anytime we go out and do something, Mina asks, How are you going to pay for this? I say, Oh, thats for NBJS. She thinks the money is coming from NBJS, who is paying the rent here. Then I dont have to worry about it. As long as you dont think its coming from me -- but eventually it all comes from me, right? At the time, I feel it didnt come from the Lord; it came from this Devata, this source.
Bhagavan says all the sources eventually merge into me. Wherever you are, whatever Devata you are worshipping, wherever the results come from, they all come from me. Apply yourself in a field of productive potential and you shall get results.
But know that all these results come from me. Antavattu phalam tesham tat bhavati alpamedhasam. But the Alpa Medhas, those with limited intellect, get finite results.
Antavattu -- which has an end. No matter how hard I try for something and get it, the joy will only last for a certain period of time. My standard example: buying a BMW.
You bought the BMW, and that joy has ended. The pursuit has its own charm. Once you reach the destination, the whole excitement of the journey has ended.
Whatever Devatas you are worshipping, certainly you will get success in that field. But the results are finite -- they have a beginning and an end. I want to see a Broadway show I have never seen in my life.
Next time Im in New York, I want to see it. But it has a beginning and an end. The show starts and ends.
After that, Im back to square one. Bhagawan said, these people with limited intellect think their destination lies in finite happiness. Therefore they pursue this field of finite happiness, and they get it.
Devan devayajo yanti mad bhakta yanti mam api. Those seeking small gains get small gains. The one who wants to hit the jackpot strives for that and reaches there sooner or later.
Bhagavan said, the Bhaktas of various Devatas -- all of us who have this desire and that -- continuously pursue them. And because we put in our efforts, we get them. But Bhagavan says, the one who seeks me finds me -- as simple as that.
Gandhiji could have been the most successful barrister in South Africa and could have made all that money like the other Gujaratis at the time. But he wasnt happy with that finite result. We would have never heard about Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi. Successful barrister, practiced in Durban and died. We would have had nothing to do with him.
But he wasnt going after the small results. He was going after what he thought rightfully belongs to his countrymen. So he became immortal.
He got what he sought after. Thats why I say be careful in what you think you want. You have this unlimited potential of realizing yourself.
But we are happy with small results in our life. Even in Sadhana, they say when you start meditating, Siddhis come to you, and youre pretty happy with that. A good example is Yoga.
In this country, Yoga is only for the physical. Patanjali didnt write the Yoga Sutras just to make your body fit. He wrote it to achieve the highest.
But we are pretty happy with the little results we get. Therefore Bhagawan says they have a limited intellect regarding where their happiness lies. They pursue fields of action, fields of potential gain, and they get results.
But those results have a beginning and an end. Inherently we are seeking infinite happiness, but we are applying ourselves in very small, finite fields of action and expecting to get infinite happiness. And therefore we oscillate between sorrow and happiness, sorrow and happiness.
Mad Bhakta Yanti Mam Api -- only my worshipper, the one who has decided that these small gains are not good enough, who needs to find the ultimate truth that gives infinite happiness. The last verse says: Avyaktam vyaktim apannam manyante mam abuddhayah. Those with no intellect to understand the truth -- all of us who have no capacity to understand it.
Because the intellect is the only instrument we use to understand things, and the intellect is a byproduct of ignorance. Ignorance creates this perception that this limited being is me. This me -- the body, mind, and intellect -- is a product of Avidya, ignorance. This mind is me, this intellect is me. That intellect is now trying to find out who the Lord is. Im going to figure it out by reading Bhagavad Gita, then the Bible, then the Quran. In the end, Ill tell you who the Lord is. Bhagavan said, those Abuddhayah -- they think that the Avyakta, the unmanifest, has manifested.
The Lord pervading everywhere whom we cant really see, who is the substratum without which this universe cannot exist, but who is not perceptible -- they think He manifests. And therefore we have all these Bhajans about Bhagavan coming: Maine aapko dekha, Bhagavan. And then we have stories about Bhagavan appearing. If Bhagavan can come stand in front of me while I am also standing here and the rest of the world is also standing -- where is that unmanifest? Therefore he said, only the one without that understanding thinks the unmanifest can manifest.
The unmanifest remains unmanifest. But I am seeking that, so I say, Oh no, this is Bhagavan. I think one of the Bal Vihar children had probably seen pictures of monks in his house. So when Dheerananda was here, the child came to our house and then went back and said, Mom, God came to Meenantis house! Because to the little child, a one wearing a saffron robe is God.
The picture he has seen is Bhagavan. God came to Meenantis house. What does Mama say? No, no, thats not God. Thats Dheerananda. For the child, the unmanifested God has manifested. The mother said, No, no, thats just Dheerananda. We, in our limited intellect, think that God manifests as Jesus, as Krishna.
But Bhagwan said, I remain unmanifest all the time. Param bhavam ajanantah mama avyayam anuttamam. Knowing a guru, knowing a prophet, and thinking, This is it. said, If thats the case, whoever went to a temple and saw the Murti would never have to find any truth -- he found Bhagavan! And anybody who found a guru would never have to do anything -- he already found the truth. He said, No, they are just indications.
The unmanifest remains unmanifest. Our limited senses, mind, and intellect have no capacity ever to understand it.

The fruit that comes to men of limited insight is finite. This simple statement contains the key to understanding human dissatisfaction. We pursue finite goals expecting infinite satisfaction. The BMW brings joy, but it ends. The promotion brings pride, but it fades. The vacation provides relaxation, but we return to the same mind we left with. Today, examine your current pursuits: Are you investing tremendous energy in achieving something that, by its very nature, cannot provide lasting fulfillment? This is not to say you should abandon worldly goals, but recognize them for what they are, finite rewards from finite efforts.
Krishna distinguishes between those who worship lesser powers (devas) and those who worship Him directly: They who worship the lesser Powers attain them; but those who worship Me come unto Me alone. The practical application is this: whatever you consistently give your attention to, you become. Worship of money makes you wealthy but not necessarily happy. Worship of fame makes you known but not necessarily at peace. Worship of the Supreme, the unchanging Reality behind all changing forms, leads to that same unchanging peace within yourself.
The verse about the ignorant thinking the Unmanifested has taken human form challenges our comfortable religious notions. If God is omnipresent, how can He be limited to any single form? This does not deny the value of divine incarnations or teachers but invites us beyond form-worship to essence-recognition. Todays contemplation: What if every person you meet is equally a manifestation of the Divine? Not just the saints and sages, but the confused, the suffering, even those who harm others? Can you glimpse the unmanifest presence wearing these countless disguises?
